newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares recover some lost ground at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares recover some lost ground at close.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices rebound modestly at close
* Relief after slight recovery in Dow Jones Index
New Zealand share prices staged a modest recovery on Wednesday after an equally slight rebound in the U.S., where the Dow Jones index broke its two-session run of serious losses.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index gained 10.78 points to 2,218.26 on turnover worth NZ$53.4 million, following on from the Dow's 27.57-point rise to 6,611.05.
Most leaders were firmer and Lion Nathan was notable for its continued recovery, firming five to NZ$3.47 having recently traded in the low $3.20s.
Brokers also commented that Brierley Investments, one of the worst performers in Tuesday's sell-off, was recovering, gaining two to NZ$1.31.

Duncan Rutherford at ANZ Securities said there was an air of general relief that U.S. stocks had shown signs of stabilising but that it would take several more steady days in the U.S. for the local market to regain its composure.
"The market is certainly a lot better after yesterday. I guess taking a sigh of relief," he said.
"But I would say the change in trend is not going to take off from here. If the Dow is down again tonight we might struggle again tomorrow and the days after."
Outside the leading stocks, fishing company Sanford gained eight to NZ$2.80, with a line of 274,500 shares transacted at that price.
Agricultural products manufacturer Donaghys dropped 20 cents to NZ$2.80, but brokers said the light volume suggested little could be read into the sudden movement.
